docs.select.a11y.chevron: The chevron is decorative: it is hidden from screen readers and ignores the pointer, so a click on it reaches the select.
docs.select.a11y.describedby: The hint and the error are linked with aria-describedby, the error first, so a screen reader says what is wrong before the help. Ids of your own are added after them.
docs.select.a11y.disabled: Disabled and unavailable are different. A disabled select leaves the tab order and is not sent. An unavailable one, with aria-disabled="true", keeps the focus and is read as unavailable, but the browser still lets it change: your handler has to ignore the change.
docs.select.a11y.error: An error sets aria-invalid and does not rely on color: the message is text under the field, and the border changes too.
docs.select.a11y.focus: The focus ring shows with the keyboard and is never removed. Keep it visible if you restyle the select.
docs.select.a11y.label: The label is visible and linked to the select, so it is what a screen reader says and what the user clicks to focus the field.
docs.select.a11y.native: It is a native select: the keyboard, the typeahead, the screen-reader behavior and, on a phone, the picker of the system are the ones of the browser, and the options are plain option elements.
docs.select.api.announce: Whether a screen reader announces the error when it appears. assertive, the default, renders it with role="alert": use it in a form that people fill in. off shows the error without announcing it, and the field stays invalid and described by it: use it for a specimen or a page that mounts fields with an error nobody caused.
docs.select.api.ariaDescribedby: Native: ids of other text that describes the select. They are joined after the error and the hint.
docs.select.api.ariaDisabled: Native: "true" dims the select and shows the not-allowed cursor, and it keeps the focus. It does not stop a change.
docs.select.api.ariaInvalid: Native: error is the only thing that sets it, so a value of your own is overwritten.
docs.select.api.children: Native: the option and optgroup elements, as in HTML.
docs.select.api.className: Added to the select, after the library's own class names.
docs.select.api.error: The error message. It marks the field as invalid, takes the red style and is announced when it appears, unless announce is off.
docs.select.api.fieldClassName: Class name of the container of the field. className goes to the select.
docs.select.api.hint: Permanent help text under the field. The select is described by it.
docs.select.api.id: Native: the label points at it. One is generated when you leave it out.
docs.select.api.label: The visible label of the field. It is what names the select.
docs.select.api.others: Every other attribute of the native select element goes to it as it is: name, value, defaultValue, onChange, disabled, required, aria-*, the event handlers and ref.
docs.select.limit.ariaDisabled: aria-disabled only dims the select and says that it is unavailable. It does not stop a change, and the value is still sent: ignore the change in onChange, or use disabled if the focus may leave.
docs.select.limit.design: The size of the chevron, and the room that the select keeps for it, come from the token --control-icon-size. Resolve, where the component comes from, wrote that 20 px in its stylesheet.
docs.select.limit.errorAnnouncement: An error is announced when it appears on a page that is already open. One that is there from the first render may not be announced on its own: it is read with the field, through aria-describedby. Set announce to off to show an error that nobody caused, as these specimens do, without announcing it.
docs.select.limit.native: It is the native element: the open list is drawn by the browser and cannot be styled, and a list of several choices (multiple, or a size above 1) is not designed.
docs.select.limit.readOnly: There is no read-only select: the browser ignores readOnly on it. Show a value that cannot change as text, and use disabled only for a select that is not available.
docs.select.limit.size: There is one size: 40 px high, and 44 px below 768 px of width, with a 20 px chevron.
docs.select.limit.validation: It does not validate anything. The error is the text you pass, and when to show it is up to you.
docs.select.state.ariaDisabledHint: It is dimmed and keeps the focus, for a moment such as saving. Nothing stops the option from changing: ignore the change in your handler.
docs.select.state.disabledHint: It is not focusable and a form does not send its value.
docs.select.state.focusHint: Reach it with Tab: a ring appears around it, and the arrow keys change the option.
docs.select.states.description: The states that Select has today. Disabled and unavailable are different states: a disabled select leaves the tab order, an unavailable one (aria-disabled) is dimmed and keeps the focus.
docs.select.states.note: A select has no read-only state: the browser ignores readOnly on it. There is no loading state either.
docs.select.summary: A native select with its visible label, its hint and its error, linked to it and drawn like Input.
docs.select.usage.description: Import Select and give it a label and the option elements as children, as in HTML. A hint and an error are linked to it for screen readers.
